**Heke tu derî vekî, gur tê.** If you open the door, the wolf will come in. After **heke** or **eger** (if) the verb takes the bi- form; what follows is in the present or the future.

- The bi- form of “to be” is **bim, bî, be, bin**: *Heke tu birçî bî, bixwe!* If you’re hungry, eat!
- *Eger baran bibare, em ê li malê bimînin.* If it rains, we’ll stay at home.

**Wî got ku ew birçî ye.** He said he was hungry. Kurdish reports speech with **ku** and keeps the speaker’s own tense: *Wî got ku ew ê bê.* He said he would come.
